description.value: Lifeboats behind Chains: Objective: launch the reef rescue. Settle the older wreck debt or free boats under witnesses; delay strands more sailors.

name.value: A Seal with the Wrong Date

description.value: A Seal with the Wrong Date: Objective: establish civilian cargo rights. Compare authentic orders or verify treatment inventory; delay claims the crates as prizes.
The Island Sings Your Name: Objective: identify an unwilling route bond. Read name ribbons or ask the choir; delay drags the beach toward the storm.
The Wreck before This Wreck: Objective: restore forgotten rescue duties. Hear survivors or recover the prize account; delay divides the flotilla.
Inspection without Impressment: Objective: move cargo under neutral witnesses. Gather both-shore inspectors or open a water transfer; delay forces crew service.

name.value: An Anchor the Island Never Chose

description.value: An Anchor the Island Never Chose: Objective: plan safe release. Mark the lower shackle or let the choir choose a current; delay wakes the chain giant.
Soundings through Broken Reef: Objective: reach stranded crews. Repair the lead line or stage low-draft crossings; delay raises the tide.
Orders aboard the Flagship: Objective: stop unlawful seizure. Deliver the authentic order or expose the false copy; delay authorizes the gun crew.
The Borrowed Verse: Objective: release unoffered names. Withdraw ribbons or preserve only volunteered route words; delay feeds the chart leech.

name.value: The Light that Must Stay Lit

description.value: The Light that Must Stay Lit: Objective: locate the last rescue group. Restore signal oil or post a witnessed lookout; delay hides survivors from the ledger.
Crates across Open Water: Objective: deliver to both shores safely. Use the neutral cradle or accept bounded inspection; delay loses a treatment window.
Under the Moving Keel: Objective: cut the private anchor. Use the calm dive or release its deck lock; delay closes the safe current.
Spoils after Rescue: Objective: revise crew obligations. Fund shared lifeboats or bind a witnessed rescue covenant; delay renews the prize dispute.
A Transfer Worth Defending: Objective: preserve civilian independence. Record both-shore deliveries or reject forced escort terms; delay presses another crew.
The Course Offered Freely: Objective: navigate without stolen names. Sing a volunteered verse or follow the choir's witness chart; delay sells the island's route.
Boats for the Next Storm: Objective: settle the free cove's future. Share rescue access or assign accountable watch crews; record costs and survivors.
Neither Navy's Prize: Objective: settle the cargo legacy. Maintain neutral inspection or independent delivery records; record both shores' needs.

name.value: An Island with Its Own Horizon

description.value: An Island with Its Own Horizon: Objective: settle living navigation. Keep an unowned chart or a revocable voyage pact; record the choir's chosen course.
Reef Distress: a stranded crew signals while free captains argue over locked boats.
Seal at the Quay: treatment crates receive a suspicious blockade claim.
Borrowed Name Song: the moving island repeats a sailor's unoffered name.
Wreck Debt: survivors of an older capture ask why rescue duties vanished.
Treatment Count: the inventory shows urgent need on both rival shores.
Current Turn: the private anchor pulls the island toward a storm mouth.
Shallow Sounding: a low-draft rescue route appears before the tide rises.
Order Comparison: the flagship copy contradicts the harbor's forged extension.
Choir Petition: islanders ask to choose a course without permanent navigation rights.
Signal Darkens: a saboteur removes oil from the reef tower.
Inspection Offer: both shores propose neutral witnesses instead of soldiers.
Released Name: a withdrawn ribbon makes the island pause before its next verse.
Boat Bargain: Tessa offers chain release under a witnessed rescue settlement.
Courier Race: the authentic order must cross open water before the gun crew fires.
Calm Window: the lower anchor shackle becomes reachable for one short dive.
Crew Places: the flotilla must choose cargo capacity and rescue seats openly.
Press Gang: an escort officer claims the neutral transfer requires crew service.
Living Chart: the next route entry changes when a sailor offers their own verse.
Survivor Hearing: Dev names people missing from the captain's prize account.
Treatment Loaded: the crates leave under a two-shore civilian receipt.
Storm Opens: the mouth allows a route sung without stolen names.
Last Rescue: the reef signal locates a final group after the harbor closes.
Extension Revoked: the commander withdraws the forged blockade claim publicly.
Anchor Cut: the island enters the chosen current without a private berth.
Ledger Revised: prize crews accept or refuse future rescue duties.
Both Shores Served: neutral deliveries change who trusts the free crews.
Choir Departure: the moving island chooses who may travel with its song.
Boats for the Next Storm: the rescue covenant sets access after the current crisis.
A Cargo Still Civilian: inspection records preserve the transfer's independent purpose.
The Unfixed Horizon: the chart follows a living island rather than owning its route.
